title: One Borrowed Knife Saved a Whale Shark 🦈
short_title: One Borrowed Knife Saved a Whale Shark 🦈
title_options: One Borrowed Knife Saved a Whale Shark 🦈
Divers Freed the Biggest Fish on Earth 🦈
A Rope Was Cutting Into a Whale Shark 🦈
seo_intro:
Divers freed a young whale shark trapped in a thick rope off Waikiki, Hawaii, in November 2026, using a knife borrowed from a nearby boat.
The rope was cutting into her fins; she stayed at the surface for the 30 minutes it took to cut her loose. Whale sharks, the biggest fish on Earth, are endangered.
sources_text: Hawaii News Now, "Divers free tangled whale shark off Waikiki" (2026-11-12); KHON2, "Rare Waikiki whale shark rescue becomes valuable discovery" (November 2026); PBS NOVA and Hawaii DLNR (sharks can't swim backward); IUCN Red List (whale shark listed as Endangered since 2016)

Off Waikiki, divers found a young whale shark, the biggest fish on Earth, trapped in a rope that was cutting into her fins 🦈 Sharks can't swim backward, so she couldn't free herself. A diver borrowed a knife from a nearby boat, and she stayed right there at the surface for the 30 minutes it took to cut her free.
